task_2.title: Restore interactive stdin under libedit-based Python 3.13+ runtimes
task_2.description: Pytest 8.3.5 fixes broken interactive input in Python 3.13+ environments that use a libedit-backed readline implementation, such as macOS and some uv-managed python-build-standalone interpreters. The update restores responsive debugger prompts and correct stdin reads when capture is temporarily suspended.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that interactive terminal input remains usable under pytest in Python 3.13+ environments that use libedit-backed readline, so debugger prompts and explicit stdin reads do not become empty or nonresponsive when capture is involved.

expectation.grounded: Pytest should preserve working stdin behavior in Python 3.13+ runtimes affected by libedit-backed readline handling. Running with `--pdb` or stopping at a breakpoint should expose a responsive `Pdb` prompt, and calling `input()` after `CaptureManager.suspend_global_capture(in_=True)` should read and return the user's entered text rather than acting empty or hanging. The startup path should remain tolerant of environments where `readline` is not importable.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to interact with pytest normally in affected Python builds: debugger sessions must accept input, and temporarily disabling capture must allow standard input reads to work as expected.

constraints.grounded: The fix must apply during pytest startup before interactive capture-dependent workflows begin, must not require users to change how they invoke `--pdb`, breakpoints, or `input()`, and must not fail startup when the `readline` module is absent.
constraints.conceptual: The behavior change should be automatic, limited to restoring correct terminal interaction, and should not introduce new setup requirements or break environments that do not provide readline support.

behavior: In Python 3.13+ environments whose interactive input stack is backed by libedit, pytest no longer leaves `Pdb` prompts unresponsive when debugging is entered through `--pdb` or breakpoints.
When global capture is suspended for stdin-aware interaction, `input()` reads the user's typed value and returns it correctly instead of producing an empty result or broken prompt behavior.
The compatibility fix is applied as part of pytest initialization so affected runtimes behave correctly before capture-managed interaction begins.
If `readline` is unavailable, pytest continues startup without raising an import failure from this compatibility handling.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is run on an affected Python 3.13+ libedit-based interpreter and execution enters `Pdb`, the debugger prompt should accept user input normally.
When pytest temporarily suspends capture with stdin enabled and application or plugin code calls `input()`, it should return the text entered by the user.
When the interpreter does not expose an importable `readline` module, pytest should still start and run without an added startup error from this fix.
When pytest runs on supported platforms and interpreter builds, the fix should require no changes to existing user commands or debugging workflows.

task_3.title: Fix pytest importlib mode stdlib name collision crash
task_3.description: Pytest 8.3.5 fixes a regression introduced in 8.3.4 where test collection could crash in importlib import mode if a project's top-level package or directory shared its name with an already-imported standard library module. The update restores successful collection and import resolution for those layouts without requiring users to rename their code.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` does not crash during collection when project code or tests live under a top-level package or directory whose name matches a standard library module.

expectation.grounded: When pytest imports test modules via `--import-mode=importlib`, it must correctly handle cases where the parent module name is already present in `sys.modules` but refers to a non-package standard library module. If that existing parent lacks package semantics, pytest should resolve the target module from the filesystem-backed project path instead of failing with `AttributeError` during submodule spec lookup.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should continue collecting and importing tests normally in importlib mode even when a project's top-level module name collides with a standard library module, rather than crashing because Python treats the existing standard library module as the parent.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve normal `--import-mode=importlib` behavior for valid package parents, only treating an already-loaded parent as unsuitable when it cannot act as a package for submodule resolution. The observable outcome should be successful import/collection instead of an `AttributeError` caused by missing package path information.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrowly scoped to the name-collision regression and must not break existing importlib-mode collection behavior for projects whose package structure already works.

behavior: Pytest recognizes that an existing top-level module with the same name as the requested project package is not a usable parent for submodule imports if it is not a package.
In `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest falls back to importing based on the project path when such a non-package parent module would otherwise be reused.
Collection/import no longer aborts with `AttributeError` in projects whose top-level package name collides with a standard library module.
acceptance_criteria: When a project uses `--import-mode=importlib` and its tests are located under a top-level package named the same as a standard library module, pytest should collect and import those tests without raising `AttributeError`.
When the colliding standard library module is already imported before collection starts, pytest should still resolve the project's filesystem-backed package hierarchy correctly.
When the parent module already represents a valid package, importlib-mode collection should continue to behave as before.

task_1.title: Honor -vv for full sequence assertion output
task_1.description: Pytest 8.3.5 fixes assertion failure reporting so very-verbose output no longer shortens sequence representations in rewritten assertion explanations when full detail is requested. This restores the expected debugging experience for large lists, dictionaries, and similar sequences while preserving normal truncation behavior at lower verbosity levels.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that assertion failure output respects very-verbose mode and shows full sequence contents instead of shortened representations when `-vv` is used.

expectation.grounded: When pytest renders rewritten assertion explanations and `-vv` results in an unlimited representation size, sequence-like objects should be formatted with an unlimited safe representation rather than the size-limited `saferepr` path. Assertion output should therefore include full list and dictionary contents in user-visible explanations, including nested `where`/expression context such as values shown for `len(...)`, while still escaping embedded newlines for single-line reporting.
expectation.conceptual: At very high verbosity, pytest should stop abbreviating sequence values in assertion failure reports and instead show the complete contents that caused the failure. Users should be able to inspect the real value directly from the failure output without losing detail to truncation.

constraints.grounded: This change should only affect cases where verbosity requests an unlimited representation size. Existing truncation behavior for normal and lower-verbosity output should remain intact, and assertion rendering should continue to sanitize multi-line representations into a safe display form.
constraints.conceptual: Only the high-verbosity reporting path should become more detailed. Standard failure output should stay compact, and the formatting should remain stable and readable even when values would otherwise span multiple lines.

behavior: When pytest is run with `-vv`, rewritten assertion explanations should display full representations of large sequences instead of shortened forms with ellipses.
The expanded representation should apply to values surfaced inside assertion context, not only direct equality diffs, so users can see complete sequence values in related explanatory output.
When verbosity does not request unlimited detail, pytest should continue using its normal size-limited safe representation for assertion output.
Sequence representations included in assertion explanations should remain safe for terminal display, including normalization of embedded newlines.
acceptance_criteria: When a failing assertion report includes a large list or dictionary and pytest is run with `-vv`, the report should show the full sequence contents rather than an abbreviated representation.

When a failure explanation includes contextual values derived from expressions such as `len(sequence)`, running with `-vv` should expose the complete underlying sequence value in the explanatory output.
When the same failures are reported without very-verbose mode, pytest should still be allowed to shorten long sequence representations.
When displayed values contain line breaks, the rendered assertion explanation should remain safely formatted for terminal output rather than injecting raw multi-line representations unexpectedly.

task_5.title: Handle deleted directories during collection
task_5.description: Pytest 8.3.5 fixes a collection-time race where a directory selected for discovery can disappear before scanning starts. Missing directories are now treated as empty during collection so the run does not crash, while unrelated filesystem errors still surface normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not crash during collection when a directory selected for discovery is removed before it can be scanned.

expectation.grounded: Update collection behavior so `_pytest.pathlib.scandir()` returns an empty result when the target directory no longer exists at scan start, allowing collection to proceed. Preserve existing error handling for directory entries so ignorable filesystem issues are skipped and non-ignorable `OSError` conditions still raise.
expectation.conceptual: If the filesystem changes during collection and a candidate directory disappears, pytest should continue gracefully by treating that location as empty instead of failing the entire run. It should still report real filesystem problems rather than suppressing them.

constraints.grounded: Only the directory-not-found condition at the start of scanning should be normalized to an empty result. Existing handling for broken entries and other scan-time errors must remain intact, including propagation of non-ignorable `OSError` cases.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to vanished directories and must not hide unrelated collection or filesystem failures.

behavior: When directory scanning begins for a path that has already been removed, scanning yields no entries instead of raising `FileNotFoundError`.
Pytest collection no longer crashes solely because a previously collected directory disappears during the collection race window.
Filesystem issues encountered while inspecting directory entries continue to follow prior semantics: ignorable ones are skipped, and non-ignorable `OSError` exceptions are still surfaced.
acceptance_criteria: Given a directory that pytest intends to collect, when that directory is deleted before scanning starts, then pytest should continue collection without crashing because the directory is treated as empty.
When a scanned directory exists but contains entries with ignorable filesystem issues, pytest should continue skipping those entries as before.
When scanning encounters a non-ignorable filesystem error unrelated to the directory simply being absent, pytest should still raise the error.

task_6.title: Add dedicated pytest typing guidance
task_6.description: Pytest 8.3.5 adds dedicated user-facing documentation explaining how to use static typing with pytest, including typing tests and fixtures. The provided code diff contains no runtime changes, so the update is documentation-only and does not alter pytest execution behavior or public API semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users upgrading to pytest 8.3.5 have a dedicated, discoverable source of guidance for using static types with pytest, including how to annotate tests and fixtures, without changing existing runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: Pytest documentation should include a dedicated 'Typing in pytest' page or equivalent guidance that explains how to use types with pytest, specifically covering how to type tests and fixtures. Because the code diff for 8.3.4 to 8.3.5 is empty, this update should not introduce observable changes to pytest runtime behavior, public APIs, warnings, or exception behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to find official guidance on applying static typing in normal pytest usage, especially for test functions and fixtures. Upgrading to this version should improve documentation only, with no change in how pytest runs.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce behavioral changes to pytest collection, execution, fixture handling, or typing-related runtime semantics as part of this update. No new runtime interfaces, errors, warnings, or altered return behavior are evidenced by the release note or code diff.
constraints.conceptual: The change should remain informational. Existing projects should behave the same after upgrading, aside from having clearer documentation about typing.

behavior: A dedicated documentation entry for using types with pytest is added for users.
The typing guidance explicitly covers how to annotate tests and fixtures.
The update does not change pytest runtime behavior, public API behavior, warnings, or errors in this area.
acceptance_criteria: When users browse pytest 8.3.5 documentation, they can access a dedicated page or section focused on typing in pytest.
When users read that page, it explains typing usage for both test functions and fixtures.
When users upgrade from 8.3.4 to 8.3.5, pytest runtime behavior remains unchanged with respect to typing-related execution semantics.

task_4.title: Fix importlib-mode ImportError for same-name namespace and module paths
task_4.description: Pytest 8.3.5 fixes a regression from 8.3.4 where `--import-mode=importlib` could resolve the wrong import target and raise `ImportError` when a directory and a Python module shared the same name. The update narrows module spec lookup for normal importers while preserving assertion rewriting for file-backed modules.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest can collect and import tests in `--import-mode=importlib` without raising `ImportError` when the project layout contains a directory and a `.py` module with the same name, including cases where tests live under that directory.

expectation.grounded: When pytest runs with `--import-mode=importlib`, it should resolve module specs so that a same-named directory and Python module are distinguished correctly instead of causing the wrong target to be imported. In these layouts, pytest should treat the parent import as the namespace/package and the fully qualified child import as the file-backed module, while preserving assertion rewriting for file-backed modules handled by pytest's assertion-rewrite importer.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run pytest in importlib mode against projects that combine namespace-style directories and same-named module files, and pytest should import the intended modules instead of crashing.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not disable assertion rewriting for file-backed modules imported through `--import-mode=importlib`, and it should remain limited to import resolution behavior needed to avoid the `ImportError` regression in same-name directory/module layouts.
constraints.conceptual: The change should remove the crash without regressing existing importlib-mode behavior, especially normal module loading and assertion rewriting in unaffected projects.

behavior: In `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest should no longer let normal meta-path spec resolution confuse a namespace-like directory with a same-named Python module nested under it.

When both a directory and a `.py` module share the same name in the import path, pytest should resolve the parent qualified name to the namespace/package view and the more specific qualified name to the actual module file.
Pytest should continue to support assertion rewriting for file-backed modules even after narrowing spec lookup to avoid the regression.
Projects matching this naming-collision layout should complete collection and import in importlib mode without raising `ImportError` as a result of the mis-resolution.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is executed with `--import-mode=importlib` in a project where a directory contains a Python file with the same base name, it should collect and import tests without failing with `ImportError` due to that naming collision.

When tests import through a parent namespace/package and then a same-named child module beneath it, pytest should resolve each qualified import to the intended target rather than swapping the namespace/package and module roles.
When the imported target is a file-backed module in importlib mode, pytest should still apply assertion rewriting behavior.
When the project does not rely on the conflicting same-name layout, importlib-mode behavior should remain unchanged from the user's perspective.

task_7.title: Preserve pytest terminal-color compatibility with Pygments 2.19+
task_7.description: Version 8.3.5 addresses a compatibility issue noted in the release note for environments using Pygments 2.19 or newer. The provided materials do not include any production-source changes, so the upgrade should be treated as an internal compatibility fix intended to keep existing terminal color and code-highlighting behavior stable rather than introducing new runtime features or API changes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.3.5 does not introduce incompatibilities with Pygments 2.19 or newer for terminal colorized output and highlighted source rendering, while preserving the existing user-visible behavior of pytest's terminal reporting.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.3.5 should remain compatible with Pygments versions 2.19 and above for terminal reporting paths that depend on syntax highlighting and ANSI color sequences. No new public API, option, warning type, or exception behavior is evidenced by the provided code diff, and the expected outcome is preservation of the established behavior of terminal output rather than a new interface.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should be able to run pytest with modern Pygments versions without seeing changed or degraded terminal reporting behavior. The patch should act as a compatibility stabilization update, not as a feature change.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new public configuration requirements, new command-line flags, or changed error and warning contracts. Keep existing terminal color and code-highlighting behavior stable for users; the provided code diff does not justify any broader runtime or API change claims.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be safe and non-disruptive. It should preserve current behavior and avoid forcing users to change how they invoke or configure pytest.

behavior: Compatibility with Pygments 2.19+ is expected to be preserved for pytest terminal output that uses syntax highlighting and ANSI color formatting.
No new end-user API surface or runtime workflow change is evidenced by the provided production diff.
The update should be interpreted as maintaining existing observable terminal-reporting behavior under newer Pygments versions, rather than changing that behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is used in an environment with Pygments 2.19 or newer, it should continue to produce terminal reporting consistent with prior supported behavior.

When colorized or highlighted terminal output is shown, the upgrade should not require users to change command-line usage, configuration, or dependency pinning solely to preserve existing output behavior.
When upgrading from 8.3.4 to 8.3.5, users should not observe any newly introduced public API, warning, or exception contract related to this change.

task_8.title: Restore Sphinx docs build compatibility with modern Towncrier
task_8.description: Version 8.3.5 restores compatibility between the project's Sphinx documentation build process and Towncrier releases from 2024, so documentation generation works again with current supported Towncrier versions. This change affects documentation tooling rather than the library's runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that building the project's Sphinx documentation works again with Towncrier versions released in 2024 and does not require users to downgrade to older Towncrier releases solely for docs generation.

expectation.grounded: When the project documentation is built with Sphinx using the sphinxcontrib.towncrier extension, Towncrier versions released in 2024 must be accepted and operate compatibly again. The upgrade should restore docs-build compatibility with modern Towncrier releases without changing the library's public runtime API.
expectation.conceptual: Documentation builds should work with current Towncrier releases again. Users maintaining docs should be able to use modern Towncrier versions without hitting a version-compatibility problem introduced in the previous release.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new runtime-facing behavior changes, public API changes, or non-documentation feature changes as part of this update. Preserve existing Sphinx documentation generation behavior aside from re-enabling compatibility with newer Towncrier versions.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to documentation tooling compatibility. The upgrade should not alter normal library usage, application behavior, or unrelated documentation outputs.

behavior: Sphinx documentation builds that rely on the Towncrier integration should support Towncrier releases from 2024 again.
Users should no longer need to pin or downgrade Towncrier to an older pre-2024 release to build documentation successfully.
The update is documentation-tooling focused and does not change the library's runtime behavior or public API surface.
acceptance_criteria: When a maintainer builds the project's Sphinx documentation with a Towncrier release from 2024, the build should proceed without a compatibility failure attributable to Towncrier version support.
When the documentation build uses the Towncrier-backed changelog integration, it should behave consistently with prior supported builds except that modern Towncrier versions are accepted again.
When upgrading from 8.3.4 to 8.3.5, users should not observe any runtime API or application behavior change outside documentation build tooling compatibility.
